description: Use this when someone asks about timing, what is coming up, or why the closing date differs from the due date. Returns the upcoming dates in order: when to pay, when each statement closes (the bureau read), and when each payment is due (the delinquency line). Calculates scenarios from supplied figures; does not make payments, change accounts, fetch external data, or retain tool inputs.

cards.description: The person's revolving credit accounts. Ask for limit, statement balance, and statement closing date per card — those three drive everything.

aprPercent.description: Purchase APR as a percentage, e.g. 19.99. Omit when unknown. Never pass 0 to mean unknown — 0 is a real interest-free rate and cost estimates would understate what a balance costs.

creditLimit.description: Credit limit in CAD. Use 0 for a charge card or any account with no set limit — it is then excluded from utilization.

currentBalance.description: Today's balance, if it differs from the statement balance. Defaults to statementBalance.

dueDate.description: Payment due date for the current statement. Defaults to 21 days after the closing date.

isOverdue.description: True if a payment is past due right now.

last4.description: Last four digits, only to tell two similar cards apart. Optional and never required.

minimumPayment.description: The issuer's minimum payment. Omit if unknown — do not pass 0 to mean unknown.

name.description: What the person calls this card, e.g. "TD Cash Back Visa" or "the blue one".

statementBalance.description: Balance at the most recent statement close. This is the figure the issuer reported, and the one utilization is read from. If only today's balance is known, pass it here and say so.

statementCloseDate.description: The day the NEXT statement closes — the date the engine targets. Found on a statement or in online banking. If omitted, a placeholder 30 days out is assumed and flagged.

count.description: How many events to return. Default 8.

today.description: Today's date in the person's local timezone, yyyy-mm-dd. Pass it — the server otherwise falls back to UTC, which is a day ahead for Canadian evenings.

name: get_statement_calendar
title: Statement calendar
